text:
Alex (Support): FYI customer reported 403 in Console after they rotated their org API key. API calls to inference endpoints work fine, but navigating to Project > Settings returns 403. Ticket #INC-1234.

Priya (Support): Can you paste repro steps and any browser console / request logs?

Alex (Support): Repro steps customer provided:
1) rotate org API key in Console
2) sign out/in (web)
3) open https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/projects/abc/settings -> 403

Curl from their post-rotation token (they redacted token):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/projects/abc/settings
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","message":"missing scope 'project:read' in token"}
```
They also pasted a snippet from browser network: `GET /api/projects/abc/members 403` and `session.id_token -> claims: { scp: "openid profile", aud: "console" }` (no project scopes).

Ken (Eng - Identity): Is that a delegated session (console exchanges org API key for a session) or a direct API key on the request? If the id_token lacks project scopes the UI will be blocked. Any chance the key rotation flow calls the proxy path that normalizes/trims scopes? We had a small change last week that affects scope propagation.

Alex (Support): Customer says the key rotation was done via the Console UI (not API). They confirmed they can use the rotated key for hosted endpoints (text/gen) using the same credentials. Only the Console UI requests fail (403).

Samir (Eng SRE): Checking auth logs for org=acme-123 around the reported time:
```
2026-03-17T14:05:12Z auth-proxy ERROR token-validation failed uid=acme-org id=org:acme-123 scopes=["hosted"] required=["project:read"] reason="scope-missing"
2026-03-17T14:05:13Z role-sync WARN backlog for org=acme-123: pending 1 job (SCIM rename stuck)
```
Looks like the session issued to the console did not receive the project scopes. My hypothesis: during key rotation the exchange path uses the compacted token flow which accidentally drops project:read/project:write scopes when the role-binding backfill is behind.

Ken (Eng - Identity): We did push a SCIM group compaction change (RWI-421) two days ago; role mapping is async and a small backlog formed overnight. If role bindings for the org are missing the scope generator will not include `project:*` scopes when minting the console session. That matches the logs.

Priya (Support): Immediate mitigation for the customer? Can we instruct them to re-login or is there something else?

Samir (Eng SRE): Two options: 1) run a manual role-sync for the org to populate role bindings immediately, then purge the auth cache so new console sessions get correct scopes; 2) short-term workaround: ask user to sign out and sign back in after ~5-10 minutes (when our background job catches up). I'll run a manual resync if we have approval.

Alex (Support): Customer wants a faster fix. Please proceed with manual resync.

Samir (Eng SRE): Running manual commands now for org acme-123 (prod):
```
# force role-sync for org
./bin/role-sync --org acme-123 --force --source=scim
# purge auth cache so console session exchange regenerates scopes
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.ai/admin/purge-auth-cache?org=acme-123" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
(Execution sanitized for thread)

ops-bot: audit-log: role-sync started org=acme-123 user=samr

ops-bot: audit-log: role-sync completed org=acme-123 added_bindings=42 removed_bindings=0 duration=12s

Ken (Eng - Identity): Good catch. I'll open a follow-up to make the rotation path idempotent w.r.t. scope propagation (PR #998). We'll also add a telemetry alert for role-sync backlog > 10.

Priya (Support): Alex — can you ask customer to try Console now?

Alex (Support): I asked them to re-open the Settings page. They just confirmed: "Settings page loads, we can see members and edit settings again" :thumbsup: They said signing out/in wasn't necessary after the purge — their session exchange picked up the updated bindings.

Alex (Support): Root cause summary posted to ticket: after org API key rotation the async role-sync backlog meant the console session exchange produced tokens without project scopes. Combined with scope-normalization change this resulted in UI 403s.

Priya (Support): Ticket updated with mitigation steps and link to postmortem (INTERNAL-PR-556). Closing once Ken's PR lands and the alert is enabled.

Ken (Eng - Identity): PR #998 merged to main, scheduled backfill tonight to ensure no other orgs affected. I'll follow up in #eng-identity with details.

Alex (Support): Customer thanked support. Marking INC-1234 resolved.

Samir (Eng SRE): Leaving note: run periodic check for role-sync queue length; create runbook item for 'UI 403 after rotation' so support can triage faster next time.
